sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 带来的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，这是一个你可以收听迷人故事、了解世界上奇妙趣事的同时还能提高英语水平的节目。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today it’s the start of another three-part mini-series, this time on “Tyrants Of The Roman Empire”.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们开始另一个三集迷你系列的节目，这次的主题是“罗马帝国的暴君”。

sentences.en: In today’s episode, we’re going to talk about the original Roman despot, the bloodthirsty, depraved, and ruthless Caligula.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们要聊聊最初的罗马暴君——那个嗜血、堕落且冷酷无情的 Caligula。

sentences.en: In part two, we’ll talk about one who wasn’t much better, the emperor who supposedly fiddled while Rome burned, Nero.
sentences.zh: 在第二部分中，我们将讨论一个好不到哪里去的皇帝——传说在罗马大火时拉琴的 Nero。

sentences.en: And in part three, we’ll be looking at Commodus.
sentences.zh: 而在第三部分中，我们将探讨 Commodus。

sentences.en: He might have been the son of Marcus Aurelius, the “philosopher emperor”, but his exploits as emperor, from claiming to be Hercules reborn to fighting in the ring as a gladiator, were not something you’d find recommended in Meditations.
sentences.zh: 他可能是“哲学家皇帝”Marcus Aurelius 的儿子，但作为皇帝，他的种种出格行径——从宣称自己是重生的 Hercules 到作为角斗士在竞技场中战斗——你在《沉思录》里是绝找不到推荐的。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into the story of Caligula.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们废话少说，直接切入 Caligula 的故事。

sentences.en: Perhaps you can think of a dinner party you’ve been to where someone around the table burst out in uncontrollable laughter.
sentences.zh: 也许你能想到自己去过的某场晚宴，席间有人突然爆发出一阵无法控制的笑声。

sentences.en: Once they composed themselves, perhaps they revealed a joke they'd just been told, or a funny story they had just heard about someone they knew.
sentences.zh: 等他们平静下来后，也许会分享刚刚听到的一个笑话，或者关于他们认识某人的趣事。

sentences.en: Others most probably joined in the merriment, and the dinner party continued as usual.
sentences.zh: 其他人多半也会加入这欢乐的气氛中，然后晚宴照常进行。

sentences.en: At one dinner party in ancient Rome, hosted by the then-emperor, Caligula, the host burst out in raucous laughter.
sentences.zh: 在古罗马的一场晚宴上，由当时的皇帝 Caligula 主办，主人突然爆发出一阵粗鲁刺耳的大笑。

sentences.en: Nobody seemed to have told the young emperor anything; nobody had slipped over on a stray grape or spilled the wine over someone’s head.
sentences.zh: 似乎没人给这位年轻的皇帝讲过什么事；没人踩在落单的葡萄上滑倒，也没人把酒洒在别人的头上。

sentences.en: There was no obvious cause for this outburst.
sentences.zh: 这次爆发没有明显的原因。

sentences.en: His consuls, who were sitting next to him, asked him why he was laughing.
sentences.zh: 坐在他身旁的执政官问他为什么笑。

sentences.en: He turned and said, "What do you suppose, except that at a single nod of mine, both of you could have your throats cut on the spot?"
sentences.zh: 他转过身说：“你们觉得呢，除了只要我点一下头，你们两个的喉咙当场就会被割断之外？”

sentences.en: We have no historical record of what happened next, but presumably a gulp from one consul, perhaps an embarrassed laugh from the other.
sentences.zh: 我们没有接下来发生事情的历史记录，但可以推测其中一个执政官咽了口唾沫，另一个则可能尴尬地笑了笑。

sentences.en: “Haha, good joke. It was a joke, right?”
sentences.zh: “哈哈，好笑。这是一个笑话，对吧？”

sentences.en: These two consuls, two of the highest elected officials of the Roman Empire, presumably knew that Caligula was deadly serious.
sentences.zh: 这两位执政官，作为罗马帝国职位最高elected officials中的两位，大概知道 Caligula 是绝对认真的。

sentences.en: A single wave of his hand or nod of his head and anyone in Rome, no matter how powerful, would be put to their death.
sentences.zh: 他只需挥一下手或点一下头，罗马的任何人，无论多么权势熏天，都会被处以死刑。

sentences.en: This was a man who revelled in public humiliation, showed little regard for human life, and held his elected officials in utter disregard.
sentences.zh: 这是一个以公开羞辱他人为乐、对人命漠不关心、对elected officials极端蔑视的人。

sentences.en: But it was not always this way, or at least, if it was always his character, he kept it well hidden.
sentences.zh: 但事情并非一向如此，或者说，如果这本来就是他的性格，他把它隐藏得很好。

sentences.en: To understand the tyranny of Caligula’s reign as emperor, we must go back to his birth, and indeed, we must remind ourselves of a little ancient Roman history.
sentences.zh: 要理解 Caligula 统治暴政，我们必须追溯到他的出生，并且，我们必须回顾一点古罗马历史。

sentences.en: As you may know, or remember from our mini-series on ancient Rome three years ago, the politics and structure of ancient Rome can be broadly divided into two: the Republic and the Empire.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能知道的，或者从我们三年前关于古罗马的迷你系列节目中记得的那样，古罗马的政治和结构大致可以分为两部分：共和国与帝国。

sentences.en: The Republic officially ended in 27 BC, and Rome became an empire, ruled by its first emperor, Augustus.
sentences.zh: 共和国于公元前27年正式结束，罗马成为了一个帝国，由其第一位皇帝 Augustus 统治。

sentences.en: Augustus was a much-loved emperor, but there was the problem of who would succeed him after his death.
sentences.zh: Augustus 是一位深受爱戴的皇帝，但存在一个问题：他死后谁来继承他？

sentences.en: A problem, as you’ll see, that crops up again and again and again in the story of Ancient Rome.
sentences.zh: 正如你将看到的，这个问题在古罗马的故事中一次又一次地出现。

sentences.en: Augustus had no biological children, but there were several stepchildren and grandchildren knocking about, some more capable than others.
sentences.zh: Augustus 没有亲生子女，但周围有几个继子和孙子，其中一些人比其他人更有能力。

sentences.en: After much manoeuvring, he named his stepson, Tiberius, as his heir on the condition that Tiberius adopt his nephew, Germanicus, as his own son, so the title of emperor would pass first to Tiberius, then to Germanicus.
sentences.zh: 经过一番周旋，他将继子 Tiberius 指定为继承人，条件是 Tiberius 必须收养他的侄子 Germanicus 为养子，因此皇帝的头衔将首先传给 Tiberius，然后传给 Germanicus。

sentences.en: In AD 14, Augustus died, and Tiberius duly became emperor.
sentences.zh: 公元14年，Augustus 去世，Tiberius 顺理成章地成为了皇帝。

sentences.en: Now, Tiberius was not exactly a people’s favourite.
sentences.zh: 现在，Tiberius 并不怎么受人民欢迎。

sentences.en: He was stern, often absent from Rome, and a man whose suspicious nature only deepened as he grew older.
sentences.zh: 他严厉，经常不在罗马，而且随着年龄的增长，他多疑的性格愈发深重。

sentences.en: He was also sadistic and bloodthirsty, and could certainly have appeared in a mini-series on tyrants, were there not others who were even more tyrannical.
sentences.zh: 他也残暴嗜血，如果不是还有比他更暴虐的人，他完全可以出现在关于暴君的迷你系列节目中。

sentences.en: Despite his relative unpopularity, his rule did provide some stability, and he would go on to rule from AD 13 to AD 37, 23 years in total.
sentences.zh: 尽管他相对不太受欢迎，但他的统治确实带来了一些稳定性，他从公元13年一直统治到公元37年，总共23年。

sentences.en: But with no direct heirs, all eyes turned, yet again, to the next generation.
sentences.zh: 但由于没有直系继承人，所有人的目光又一次转向了下一代。

sentences.en: Here, there was a clear frontrunner: Germanicus, Tiberius’ adopted son, and by this point, a decorated young man and accomplished military leader.
sentences.zh: 在这里，有一个明显的领跑者：Tiberius 的养子 Germanicus，此时他已经是一个勋功卓著的年轻人和出色的军事领袖。

sentences.en: Germanicus was everything the Romans admired: a brilliant general, a charismatic leader, and — importantly — the great-nephew of Augustus himself, so he had that all-important pedigree, the blood tie to Augustus.
sentences.zh: Germanicus 具备罗马人钦佩的一切：出色的将军、富有魅力的领袖，而且——重要的是——他本人就是 Augustus 的曾侄孙，所以他拥有至关重要的血统，与 Augustus 有血缘关系。

sentences.en: What’s more, he was married to a granddaughter of Augustus, Agrippina the Elder.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，他娶了 Augustus 的孙女大 Agrippina。

sentences.en: Together, they formed what many saw as the perfect imperial couple.
sentences.zh: 他们在一起，构成了许多人眼中的完美帝王夫妇。

sentences.en: However, tragedy struck. Germanicus, this heroic military leader who seemed poised to become the next emperor, died suddenly in Syria in AD 19, at the age of 33.
sentences.zh: 然而，悲剧降临了。Germanicus 这位似乎注定要成为下一任皇帝的英雄军事统帅，于公元19年在叙利亚突然去世，享年33岁。

sentences.en: There are rumours he was poisoned, perhaps on Tiberius’ orders, or perhaps it was one of the many bugs that could have proved fatal for travelling soldiers back then.
sentences.zh: 有传言说他是被毒死的，也许是奉了 Tiberius 的命令，或者也许只是当时对旅行中的士兵来说致命的众多病毒之一。

sentences.en: In any case, he left behind a widow and six children.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他留下了一个遗孀和六个孩子。

sentences.en: Among them was a boy named Gaius Julius Caesar Germanicus.
sentences.zh: 其中包括一个名叫 Gaius Julius Caesar Germanicus 的男孩。

sentences.en: But the soldiers had another name for him.
sentences.zh: 但士兵们给他起了另一个名字。

sentences.en: As a child, this boy would often visit his father’s military camps dressed in a tiny soldier’s outfit, complete with little leather boots.
sentences.zh: 小时候，这个男孩经常穿着一套迷你士兵制服参观他父亲的军营，脚上还穿着可爱的小皮靴。

sentences.en: The soldiers nicknamed him “Little Boots”, “Caligula” in Latin.
sentences.zh: 士兵们给他起了个外号叫“小靴子”，拉丁语就是“Caligula”。

sentences.en: Although he is believed to have hated the nickname as an adult, and never used it himself, it stuck, and I’ll continue to use it for the rest of this episode.
sentences.zh: 虽然人们认为他成年后讨厌这个外号，而且自己从未使用过，但它还是流传开了，我将在本集的其余部分继续使用这个名字。

sentences.en: Now, after Germanicus’s death, his widow openly accused Tiberius of murder, which was not a particularly smart thing to do, especially to an emperor as malicious and sadistic as Tiberius.
sentences.zh: 在 Germanicus 去世后，他的遗孀公开指控 Tiberius 谋杀，这可不是什么明智之举，特别是对像 Tiberius 这样恶毒残暴的皇帝而言。

sentences.en: She was banished, and she eventually died of starvation.
sentences.zh: 她被流放了，最终饥寒交迫而死。

sentences.en: Two of Caligula’s brothers were either imprisoned or executed.
sentences.zh: Caligula 的两个兄弟要么被监禁，要么被处决。

sentences.en: Caligula, however, survived. And not only did he survive, but when he was 19, he was brought to live with Tiberius, in Capri, just off the coast of Naples.
sentences.zh: 然而，Caligula 活了下来。不仅活了下来，在他19岁时，他被带去与 Tiberius 一起生活，地点在靠近那不勒斯海岸的卡 Capri 岛。

sentences.en: Now, Caligula knew what Tiberius stood accused of: the murder of his father, and he knew what Tiberius had done to the rest of his family.
sentences.zh: Caligula 知道 Tiberius 被指控犯下的罪行：谋杀他的父亲，他也知道 Tiberius 对他家族其他人做过的事。

sentences.en: And on the island, he also saw what fate awaited anyone who crossed the sadistic emperor: being pushed off a high cliff if they were lucky, and being slowly tortured to death if they weren’t.
sentences.zh: 在这个岛上，他也看到了任何敢于顶撞这位残暴皇帝的人将面临的命运：幸运的话被推下高高的悬崖，不幸的话则被慢慢折磨致死。

sentences.en: So, if Caligula did feel resentment towards Tiberius, which was clearly perfectly reasonable, he kept those feelings locked up inside.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果 Caligula 对 Tiberius 确实怀有怨恨，而这显然完全合情合理，他也把这种情绪深深锁在心里。

sentences.en: He flattered Tiberius; he never mentioned his father once, and he learned how to play the role of the obedient servant.
sentences.zh: 他奉承 Tiberius；他一次也没有提过自己的父亲，并且学会了扮演一个顺从的仆人。

sentences.en: When Tiberius finally died in AD 37, Caligula was 24 years old.
sentences.zh: 当 Tiberius 终于在公元37年去世时，Caligula 24岁。

sentences.en: Now, there are some rumours that Caligula murdered Tiberius, with one account having him suffocate the man with a pillow, but these are unsubstantiated.
sentences.zh: 现在，有一些传言称 Caligula 谋杀了 Tiberius，其中一种说法是他用枕头闷死了这个人，但这些都没有证实。

sentences.en: Tiberius was 77 years old, which was a ripe old age at this time, and there is simply no evidence to suggest it was anything other than natural causes.
sentences.zh: Tiberius 享年77岁，在当时这已经是高寿了，而且根本没有证据表明这是自然死亡之外的任何原因。

sentences.en: It was, of course, good news for Caligula.
sentences.zh: 这当然对 Caligula 来说是个好消息。

sentences.en: Although he was relatively unknown as an individual in Rome, and he had little knowledge of the workings of Roman politics or the Roman army, he seemed like the obvious successor.
sentences.zh: 尽管他在罗马作为个人并不为人熟知，而且他对罗马政治或罗马军队的运作知之甚少，但他似乎是显而易见的继承人。

sentences.en: He was the son of the heroic general Germanicus and the adopted grandson of Rome’s first emperor, Augustus.
sentences.zh: 他是英雄将军 Germanicus 的儿子，也是罗马第一位皇帝 Augustus 的养孙。

sentences.en: He seemed to embody a golden future, a new chapter for Rome.
sentences.zh: 他似乎体现了一个金色的未来，罗马的新篇章。

sentences.en: And, sure enough, he arrived in Rome and was hailed as emperor.
sentences.zh: 果然，他抵达罗马并被欢呼为皇帝。

sentences.en: The transition from unknown boy to commander of the world’s most powerful empire at the time was incredibly smooth.
sentences.zh: 从一个默默无闻的男孩转变为当时世界上最强大帝国的统帅，这个过渡异常平稳。

sentences.en: And for the first few months of his reign, Caligula seemed to live up to the hopes and dreams of the people of Rome.
sentences.zh: 在他的统治头几个月里，Caligula 似乎不负罗马人民的希望与梦想。

sentences.en: He threw vast gladiatorial games in celebration, he honoured all of his predecessors' last wishes, he gave every citizen of Rome a cash payment, and he made sure to double the cash payment for the Praetorian guard, the emperor’s personal armed unit.
sentences.zh: 他举办了盛大的角斗士比赛以示庆祝，他兑现了所有前任的最后遗愿，他给每个罗马公民发放了现金奖励，并且确保将禁卫军（皇帝的私人武装部队）的现金奖励翻倍。

sentences.en: He also made a big deal of publicly destroying all of Tiberius’s written records of suspected treachery among the senators, symbolically burning them, as if saying, “This was the past, tomorrow is a new day”.
sentences.zh: 他还大张旗鼓地公开销毁了 Tiberius 留下的所有关于元老院议员涉嫌叛国行为的书面记录，象征性地将它们烧毁，仿佛在说：“过去已矣，明天又是新的一天”。

sentences.en: He even said that he hadn’t read them, which would turn out to be a lie.
sentences.zh: 他甚至说自己没有读过这些记录，这后来证明是个谎言。

sentences.en: In any case, the first few months of his rule were, as one contemporary historian put it, a "Golden Age" of happiness and prosperity.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，正如一位当代历史学家所说，他统治的头几个月是一个充满幸福和繁荣的“黄金时代”。

sentences.en: But, seven months or so after becoming emperor, he fell seriously ill.
sentences.zh: 但是，在他成为皇帝大约七个月后，他生了一场重病。

sentences.en: It’s not clear what this illness was, whether he caught it randomly or whether he was poisoned in some way, but for almost a month, he was at death’s door.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚这场病是什么，他是偶然感染的还是以某种方式被下毒的，但在近一个月的时间里，他命悬一线。

sentences.en: It looked like he could have died at any moment.
sentences.zh: 看起来他随时都可能死去。

sentences.en: This being ancient Rome, senators were scurrying around making preparations, both for the eventuality that he wouldn’t recover and succumbed to his illness, and that he would make a full recovery.
sentences.zh: 既然这里是古罗马，元老院议员们便四处奔走进行筹备，既为了他未能康复而不幸离世的可能性做准备，也为了他完全康复做准备。

sentences.en: One politician, and man of noble blood, Atanius Secundus, had what he must have thought was a cunning idea.
sentences.zh: 有一位政治家、出身高贵的 Atanius Secundus 想到了一个他自己认为是精明的主意。

sentences.en: He publicly pledged that he would fight in the arena as a gladiator if only Caligula recovered.
sentences.zh: 他公开承诺，只要 Caligula 康复，他就会作为角斗士在竞技场中战斗。

sentences.en: Presumably, he thought it was a win-win situation.
sentences.zh: 大概他觉得这是一场稳赚不赔的交易。

sentences.en: If Caligula died, which seemed highly probable, he could point at how dedicated he had been to the emperor, and how he'd been willing to fight and most probably die in the arena for his cherished master.
sentences.zh: 如果 Caligula 去世了，这看起来极有可能，他就可以指出自己对皇帝是多么忠诚，为了他心爱的主人，他甚至愿意在竞技场中战斗并很可能牺牲。

sentences.en: And if Caligula made a full recovery, he would hear of this pledge and be so impressed by the man’s loyalty that he would be richly rewarded.
sentences.zh: 而如果 Caligula 完全康复，他就会听到这个承诺，并对这个男人的忠诚印象深刻，从而给予丰厚的奖励。

sentences.en: Caligula did make a full recovery, but it seems that after this return from the brink of death, something changed.
sentences.zh: Caligula 确实完全康复了，但似乎在这次从鬼门关走了一遭之后，有什么东西改变了。

sentences.en: He heard about the senator’s bold promise to fight in the arena, and told him, in no uncertain terms, “ok then, get on with it”.
sentences.zh: 他听说了这位参议员要在竞技场战斗的大胆承诺，并毫不含糊地告诉他：“好啦，那就开始吧”。

sentences.en: The man, who was not in great shape and had never held a sword before, was duly marched into the gladiatorial area and mown down by a professional gladiator.
sentences.zh: 这个人身体状况并不好，以前也从未拿过剑，于是理所当然地被押进了角斗场，被一名职业角斗士轻而易举地击杀。

sentences.en: From that point on, the honeymoon period of Caligula’s reign was well and truly over.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，Caligula 统治的蜜月期彻底结束了。

sentences.en: The generous young emperor, the son of Germanicus, the darling of Rome, seemed to vanish.
sentences.zh: 那个慷慨的年轻皇帝、Germanicus 的儿子、罗马的宠儿，似乎消失了。

sentences.en: What replaced him was a ruler who seemed to revel in cruelty, humiliation, and excess.
sentences.zh: 取代他的是一个似乎以残忍、羞辱和无节制为乐的统治者。

sentences.en: Executions became an almost daily occurrence.
sentences.zh: 处决几乎成了家常便饭。

sentences.en: He would invite senators to dine with him, serve them the finest food, and then, at the height of the feast, casually order their deaths.
sentences.zh: 他会邀请元老院议员与他共进晚餐，为他们提供最精美的食物，然后在宴会高潮时，随口下令将他们处死。

sentences.en: He delighted in seeing people squirm. Prisoners were executed in front of him for sport.
sentences.zh: 他以看着别人痛苦挣扎为乐。囚犯们为了供他消遣而在他面前被处决。

sentences.en: Sometimes he would order people slowly tortured, so he could watch their agony.
sentences.zh: 有时他会下令将人慢慢折磨，这样他就能欣赏他们的痛苦。

sentences.en: The Roman historian Suetonius even claims he enjoyed watching executions scheduled for his mealtimes as if it were a form of light entertainment.
sentences.zh: 罗马历史学家 Suetonius 甚至声称，他喜欢在用餐时间看人受刑，仿佛那是一种轻松的娱乐活动。

sentences.en: Then there were the humiliations. Senators were forced to run for long distances alongside his chariot, like stable boys rather than statesmen.
sentences.zh: 接着是羞辱。元老院议员们被迫沿着他的战车长途奔跑，与其说是国家重臣，倒不如说像马厩里的杂役。

sentences.en: And this was layered on top of the sexual depravity.
sentences.zh: 而这一切还叠加在性堕落之上。

sentences.en: He is said to have prostituted the wives of noblemen, inviting senators and their wives to banquets, then forcing the wives, one by one, into side rooms, forcing them to have sex with him and then describing their performance in intimate detail, publicly, in front of their husbands.
sentences.zh: 据说他出卖贵族们的妻子，邀请元老院议员和他们的妻子参加宴会，然后强迫这些妻子一个接一个地进入侧室，强迫她们与他发生性关系，接着在她们的丈夫面前公开、极其细致地描述她们的表现。

sentences.en: There are accounts of him creating a brothel inside the imperial palace, complete with hundreds of women and young boys.
sentences.zh: 有记录称他在皇宫内建立了一个妓院，里面有数百名妇女和年轻男孩。

sentences.en: And when it wasn’t humiliation and sexual depravity, he is also remembered by historians as an ineffective and cowardly leader of Rome.
sentences.zh: 当他不搞羞辱和性堕落时，历史学家也记住了他作为一个无能且懦弱的罗马领袖。

sentences.en: One account has him marching his troops northwards, as if to attack Great Britain, but after lining his troops up on the beach in Gaul, he orders them to collect seashells instead of continue their mission, declaring these the “spoils of the ocean”.
sentences.zh: 有一个记载说，他率领军队向北行进，仿佛要进攻英国，但在高卢的海滩上排好军队后，他却命令他们去收集贝壳而不是继续任务，并宣称这些是“海洋的战利品”。

sentences.en: To many, this became a perfect image of his reign: playing at war while humiliating Rome’s soldiers.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这成了他统治的完美写照：把战争当儿戏，同时羞辱罗马的士兵。

sentences.en: And then, perhaps most famously, came his obsession with divinity.
sentences.zh: 然后，也许最为人所知的是，他对神性的痴迷。

sentences.en: Previous and subsequent emperors became deified after death, but Caligula demanded worship in his own lifetime.
sentences.zh: 前任和后来的皇帝都是在死后才被奉为神明，但 Caligula 要求在世时就受到崇拜。

sentences.en: He had temples erected to his own glory, with priests appointed to offer sacrifices to him as though he were Jupiter.
sentences.zh: 他为自己的荣耀建造了神庙，并指定祭司向他献祭，仿佛他就是 Jupiter。

sentences.en: He appeared in public dressed as Apollo, Mercury, even Venus, the female goddess of love.
sentences.zh: 他在公众场合打扮成 Apollo、Mercury 甚至爱之女神 Venus。

sentences.en: He reportedly once appeared in the theatre dressed as Venus, complete with wig and dress, delighting in the outrage of Rome’s conservative senators.
sentences.zh: 据报道，他曾有一次打扮成 Venus 出现在剧院里，戴着假发穿着长袍，对罗马保守派元老院议员的愤怒感到洋洋得意。

sentences.en: He simply didn’t care what Roman high society thought about him; he threw money hand over fist at the Praetorian guard and knew that this money assured loyalty, and therefore protection.
sentences.zh: 他根本不在乎罗马上流社会对他的看法；他大手大脚地把钱砸给禁卫军，并且知道这些钱能确保忠诚，从而确保安全。

sentences.en: Well, it did for a while, as we’ll discover in a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实管用了一阵子，正如我们几分钟后会发现的那样。

sentences.en: Protected by a seemingly loyal imperial guard and with his ruthlessness against political enemies well known, it seemed there was nobody or nothing to stop him.
sentences.zh: 在看似忠诚的禁卫军保护下，加上他对政敌的残酷手段人尽皆知，似乎没有任何人或事能阻止他。

sentences.en: He spent lavishly, not just on himself but on public projects.
sentences.zh: 他挥霍无度，不仅在自己身上，还在公共项目上。

sentences.en: He built pleasure-galleys to cruise the Bay of Naples: vast ships with baths, colonnades, banquet-halls and even vines.
sentences.zh: 他建造了游艇去巡游那不勒斯湾：配有浴室、柱廊、宴会厅甚至葡萄藤的巨大船只。

sentences.en: In a lake just south of Rome, Lake Nemi, he launched colossal barges with marble flooring.
sentences.zh: 在罗马南部的一个湖泊 Nemi 湖中，他下水了带有大理石地板的庞大驳船。

sentences.en: As a quick side note for the seriously dedicated listeners among you, you may remember these barges from episode number 516, on the history of underwater exploration.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，对于节目中那些极其忠实的听众，你们可能还记得来自第516集关于水下探索历史的这些驳船。

sentences.en: Well done if so. Anyway, back to Caligula.
sentences.zh: 如果猜对了，做得好。言归正传，我们回到 Caligula。

sentences.en: At the start of AD 41, not even 4 years into his rule, clearly, some people were thinking enough was enough.
sentences.zh: 在公元41年初，离他上台还不到4年，显然有些人觉得够了。

sentences.en: On January 24th, AD 41, he was preparing for a trip to Alexandria, in Egypt.
sentences.zh: 公元41年1月24日，他正准备前往埃及的亚历山大港。

sentences.en: He had been doing one of his favourite activities–watching gladiatorial games–and was heading inside for a spot of lunch.
sentences.zh: 他一直在做他最喜欢的活动之一——观看角斗士比赛——并正走进去准备吃点午饭。

sentences.en: He had been told that there was a group of young boys who were practising, and could he come and spare a few words?
sentences.zh: 有人告诉他有一群年轻男孩正在练习，他能不能过去说几句话？

sentences.en: As he was about to address the boys, two of his trusted Praetorian guards pounced on him, stabbing him a total of 30 times in the neck, chest and genitals.
sentences.zh: 正当他准备对男孩们讲话时，他信任的两名禁卫军突然扑向他，在脖子、胸部和生殖器上总共捅了30刀。

sentences.en: One report even has them stripping and eating his flesh.
sentences.zh: 甚至有一份报告说他们剥光并吃掉了他的肉。

sentences.en: Caligula, “Little Boots”, was dead. Now, as for the motivations behind this assassination, there is no evidence of a wide plot among senators for moral grounds, for the purposes of “saving Rome”, or anything like that.
sentences.zh: Caligula，“小靴子”，死了。现在，关于这次暗杀背后的动机，没有证据表明元老院内部存在出于道德原因、为了“拯救罗马”或类似目的的广泛阴谋。

sentences.en: One hypothesis is that it was more personal.
sentences.zh: 一种假设是它更具个人色彩。

sentences.en: The man who is said to have landed the first blow, Cassius Chaerea, was a brave and distinguished Praetorian, but he was often teased by Caligula for having a high-pitched voice, and being effeminate in his manners.
sentences.zh: 据说刺出第一刀的人 Cassius Chaerea 是一位勇敢杰出的禁卫军，但他经常被 Caligula 取笑声音尖锐、举止娘娘腔。

sentences.en: So yes, Caligula might have been seriously unhinged and utterly inappropriate as a Roman emperor, but one theory is that he was murdered for being a bully rather than anything more strategic than that.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，Caligula 可能真的精神失常、完全不配做一个罗马皇帝，但其中一种理论认为，他被谋杀是因为他是个恶霸，而不是出于比这更具战略意义的原因。

sentences.en: And on this note, much of what we know about Caligula as a man and his reign comes down to only a few sources that were written decades after his death.
sentences.zh: 说到这里，我们对 Caligula 作为一个男人以及他的统治的了解，很大程度上归结于在他死后几十年才写成的少数几个来源。

sentences.en: These were second, often third-hand accounts, and there is little way of verifying these claims.
sentences.zh: 这些都是二手，甚至往往是三手的记载，几乎没有办法核实这些说法。

sentences.en: The most famous example is one that you might be surprised hasn’t come up yet: that he “made his favourite horse a senator”, and this is an example of how insane he was.
sentences.zh: 最著名的例子你可能感到惊讶，到现在还没出现：那就是他“把他最喜欢的马封为参议员”，这成了他如何疯狂的例证。

sentences.en: Firstly, this isn’t historically accurate, in that the historian recalling it says that Caligula suggested that he would make his horse a consul.
sentences.zh: 首先，这在历史上并不准确，因为回忆这一事件的历史学家说的是 Caligula 暗示他会把马任命为执政官。

sentences.en: And secondly, it was almost certainly a joke by Caligula, and one that the historian didn’t get.
sentences.zh: 其次，这几乎肯定是 Caligula 开的一个玩笑，而这位历史学家没有听懂。

sentences.en: We know that Caligula loved playing jokes and had a devilish sense of humour, and it seems much more probable that either he was planning on doing this to ridicule his senators, or that he made a passing comment along the lines of “so and so is so useless that my horse could govern better than they could”.
sentences.zh: 我们知道 Caligula 喜欢开玩笑，并且有着恶魔般的幽默感，似乎更有可能是他当时正计划这样做来羞辱他的元老院议员，或者他只是顺口说了一句类似“某某某太废物了，我的马都比他治理得好”这样的话。

sentences.en: He wasn’t actually planning to make his horse a senator.
sentences.zh: 他其实并没有计划真的让他的马当参议员。

sentences.en: So, to wrap things up, Caligula met his end at the hands of the men he thought he could trust.
sentences.zh: 所以，总而言之，Caligula 死在了他以为自己可以信任的人手下。

sentences.en: And they didn’t just kill him; shortly after he was killed, so too were his wife and young daughter, in order to completely eradicate all lines of succession.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不仅杀了他；在他死后不久，他的妻子和幼女也被杀害，以便彻底根除所有的继承血脉。

sentences.en: Instead, his uncle, Claudius, was made emperor, and he ruled for 13 years before the subject of the next episode, Nero, took over.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是，他的叔叔 Claudius 被立为皇帝，统治了13年，之后便是下一集的主角 Nero 接管。

sentences.en: As for Caligula, he didn’t even rule for four years, but his name is forever associated with cruelty, despotism, and the perils of unchecked absolute power.
sentences.zh: 至于 Caligula，他甚至没有统治满四年，但他的名字永远与残暴、专制以及不受约束的绝对权力的危险联系在一起。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on Caligula, the potential golden boy turned sadistic killer.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的节目就到这里，关于 Caligula，这位由金色男孩沦为嗜血杀手的暴君。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目很有趣，并且让你学到了新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I'd love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我很想知道你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: You can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接前往我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他充满好奇心的听众畅聊。

sentences.en: As a reminder, this is part one of a three-part mini-series on the theme of Roman Tyrants.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下，这是关于罗马暴君主题的三集迷你系列的第一部分。

sentences.en: Next up it’ll be Nero, and in part three, it will be Commodus.
sentences.zh: 接下来是 Nero，在第三部分中，将是 Commodus。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 带来的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，注意安全，我们下期节目见。
